name: bobcat-flash-1.1
scope: Fast Bobcat tier (typed decisions: Choice/Noul/Score). Additional tier; it replaces no released model, so no sealed final was opened.

base.architecture_note: Gemma 4 26B-A4B: 30 layers, sliding-window (1024) + global attention, 128 experts top-8 plus a dense MLP, about 4B active parameters

teacher.model: Qwen3.8-27B + Bobcat LoRA 2704495d..., merged BF16, vLLM

teacher11.model: bobcat-1.1: Qwen3.8-27B + LoRA 33a323d1..., merged BF16, vLLM

readout.contract: first answer position, offered identifier logits only, piecewise compile, closed JSON by the host

bench.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

final_evaluation.reason: Flash 1.1 is an additional tier; the fresh sealed final stays for a release that replaces a model

serving_artifacts.note: Additive serving builds and settings for the frozen adapter above. The adapter, base revision, tokenizer and every frozen field are unchanged. All figures are development measurements (product eval v2 dev, TypeSafe 20) on one RTX PRO 6000; no sealed final was opened.

derived_from.merge: bobcat.student_merge (fp32 product and sum, BF16 storage)

nvfp4.tool: scripts/nvfp4_quantize.py, llmcompressor 0.14.0 (compressed-tensors 0.19.0): NVFP4 W4A4, group 16, FP8 scales
nvfp4.calibration: 256 product-eval v2 DEV compiled prompts <= 4,096 tokens (seed 20260926); every token through every expert (moe_calibrate_all_experts); ids in bobcat-nvfp4.json and excluded from the drift rows
nvfp4.experts: 3D expert tensors linearized to one Linear per expert projection before calibration; 11,520 expert projections quantized, none BF16

health.engine: vllm (nvfp4-pack-quantized), all schedule, cached state encoding

nvfp4.status: built and measured; NOT the recommended serving build on RTX PRO 6000: slower than FP8 (44.0K vs 48.6K prompt tokens/s) and less accurate (dev and TypeSafe 20). A different numerical artifact from the evaluated adapter.

nvfp4_experts_fp8_dense_attempt.status: failed, not uploaded: the FP8 group's regex targets named `language_model.layers`, which vLLM's module names (`language_model.model.layers`) do not match, so vLLM read the FP8 tensors as unquantized weights (dev engine macro 0.375). Fixed in scripts/nvfp4_quantize.py; not rebuilt, because the kernel profile shows the NVFP4 MoE path itself is slower than FP8 here.

serving_config_recommended.precision: FP8 (vLLM online dynamic FP8 of the merged BF16 weights, --quantization fp8); the merged shards' sha256 are above
serving_config_recommended.engine: vLLM 0.30.0, TRITON_ATTN (FA4 unavailable for head dims 256/512)
serving_config_recommended.server: bobcat.flash_server, or bobcat.api_server (state tokenized once per request, same token IDs), --schedule all

moe_kernel_config.source: vLLM 0.30.0 bundled E=128,N=704 fp8_w8a8 config for the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, copied under the Server Edition name

health.engine: vllm (fp8), all schedule, cached state encoding

routing.server: bobcat.route_server: one process, Flash and Bobcat 1.1 engines on one GPU

rule.out_of_range_before_any_pass: more than 64 candidates, or fewer than 50% of letters Hangul or ASCII Latin (same 225 dev rows as the offline rule)
rule.low_confidence: Flash top probability at T=0.8912 below 0.8 (threshold chosen on the calibration split, bobcat-flash report 5.9)

routing_length_rule.note: Additive routing rule for the frozen adapter above; the adapter, base revision, tokenizer and every frozen field are unchanged (sha256 of this manifest without serving_artifacts: 88056ce0..., as bound by the final-opening record). All figures are development measurements (product eval v2 dev, TypeSafe 20) on one RTX PRO 6000; no sealed final was opened; Jev was not called.
routing_length_rule.server: bobcat.route_server --max-flash-tokens 2048 (the default; 0 turns the rule off)

rule.length: the question's Flash-compiled sequence (its state and itself, Flash tokens) longer than 2048 -> Bobcat 1.1 before any pass, beside the out-of-range rules
order: fewer than 50% of letters Hangul or ASCII Latin -> Bobcat
rule.flash_build: FP8 (online) of the merged frozen adapter, temperature 0.8911980656311957

selection.data: DEV only: the canonical 300 long-context dev questions (salt bobcat-long-context-v1) padded to Flash-token levels 0/1024/2048/3072/4096/6144/8192, plus the full dev split unpadded (3,188)
selection.scores: engine-level logits of the two served builds (vLLM 0.30.0, max_model_len 32832), the identical padded request text for both
selection.constraint: routed quality >= Bobcat 1.1 alone - 1.0 pt at every level (point estimates)
selection.choice_rule: largest qualifying T (most questions on Flash)

holdout_reported_only.note: a disjoint 300-question dev sample; at T=2048 it misses the 1 pt margin at the unpadded and 1K levels (-1.33 pt, 4 of 300 questions), where the length rule routes nothing: the gap is the confidence rule's

measured_http_server_host.client: loopback HTTP on the server host, one request per question (server-side, not a separate same-AZ client)

typesafe20.question_lengths_flash_tokens: 418 questions: median 5,268, max 11,094; 71.5% longer than 2048 (invoice 100%, security 92%, agent trace 64%, customer service 0%)

routing_length_rule.trade_off: the rule sends every question longer than 2048 Flash tokens to Bobcat 1.1: on TypeSafe 20 Flash answers 21.5% of the questions (82.8% without the rule), so long-state workflows run at Bobcat cost; short dev traffic is unchanged (Flash 84.0%).
routing_length_rule.status: recommended routing rule for the Flash -> Bobcat 1.1 route server (quality tier); Flash alone is unchanged
routing_length_rule.server_source_note: sha256 of the shipped route_server.py (default --max-flash-tokens 2048). The measurements ran an earlier revision of the same change whose default was off, started with --max-flash-tokens 2048; the rule code was the same.

merged_bf16.note: Additive ready-to-serve checkpoint of the frozen adapter above (to be published as sanghwa-na/bobcat-flash-1.1). The adapter, base revision, tokenizer and every frozen field are unchanged (sha256 of this manifest without serving_artifacts: 88056ce0..., as bound by the final-opening record). No sealed final was opened; Jev was not called.
merged_bf16.merge: bobcat.student_merge in the serving environment (vLLM 0.30.0, torch 2.13.0): each of the 235 adapted weights becomes bf16(W + (alpha/r) B A), alpha/r = 2.0, with the product and sum in float32; every other tensor and file of the base is copied
merged_bf16.identical_to_served_merge_note: the shard hashes equal serving_artifacts.nvfp4.derived_from.merged_shards_sha256, the merge behind the FP8 serving figures and the NVFP4 study
merged_bf16.serving: vLLM 0.30.0 loads it with --quantization fp8 (online dynamic FP8), as measured; see serving_config_recommended

equivalence_to_adapter_path.sample: every 10th row of the compiled product-eval v2 dev split (319 decisions: search 86, citation 55, document screening 55, routing 55, classification 50, tool call 18)
equivalence_to_adapter_path.paths: BF16 base + unmerged LoRA (bobcat.flash_train --eval-only --init adapter) vs this checkpoint (same code, no adapter), one RTX PRO 6000, HF transformers 5.17.0
equivalence_to_adapter_path.changed_answers_note: all five are search near-ties (top two within 0.08 on the adapter path)

merged_bf16.status: ready-to-serve weights; the served (FP8) figures of this manifest are this checkpoint's

fp8.note: Additive pre-quantized FP8 checkpoint for the Bobcat Flash Space (to be published as sanghwa-na/bobcat-flash-1.1-fp8); the adapter, base revision, tokenizer and every frozen field are unchanged. No sealed final was opened; Jev was not called.
fp8.derived_from: the merged BF16 checkpoint in merged_bf16 (downloaded from sanghwa-na/bobcat-flash-1.1 and checked against its SHA256SUMS)
fp8.tool: scripts/fp8_quantize.py (llm-compressor 0.14.0, transformers 5.17.0, torch 2.13.0): FP8_DYNAMIC, float8_e4m3fn weights with one scale per output channel, activations quantized per token at run time (no calibration data); compressed-tensors format (vLLM: --quantization none); the 30 fused expert blocks linearized into one Linear per expert first (11,520 expert projections quantized)
fp8.kept_bf16: lm_head, embeddings, norms, the 30 routers, the vision tower (205 dense and 11,520 expert projections quantized)

typesafe20_served.server: bobcat.flash_server --quantization none, vLLM 0.30.0, one RTX PRO 6000, localhost HTTP

fp8.status: a different numerical artifact from the evaluated adapter; the figures above are its own

public_copy.changes: storage locations, cost figures, host and instance details, internal report and orchestration paths, and results of models other than this release and its untrained base removed; the NVFP4 quantizer named by its public path, scripts/nvfp4_quantize.py; nothing else changed
